turns.text: ok be honest how do i tell my husband he doesnt have to take every overtime shift. its voluntary-ish at his job but he takes all of them. and i dont want it to sound like money is tight lol. i just got back from ruiz family market for tomorrows cooking and stayed under budget so im in a good mood about it

Nice work on the budget. Short version: make it about him and about the two of you, not the numbers.

Things that work:
- Pick a calm moment, not when he's just walked in or is half asleep.
- Lead with what you've noticed: "You've been getting home wiped out and falling asleep early. I miss having you around."
- Frame it as a choice, not a rule: "You don't have to say yes to every one. Maybe pick the ones you actually want."
- Offer something instead: a dinner together, a free evening, a weekend morning.

Sample wording: "Hey, I've noticed the ten-hour days are wearing you out. I'd rather have you rested and around more. What if you skipped a couple each month?"

Avoid: "we can't afford," "I'm worried about," or anything that sounds like checking his work.

ok thats good. i wont mention the bills at all. he gets weird about being the provider. also my back is sore i just finished my saturday shift at the senior lunch at the community center, 18 an hour, it helps a little

Good call keeping it off the bills. Your shift is also a natural opener, since you're pitching in without making it a big deal.

You could say: "I'm picking up my Saturdays and it's working out fine, so you've got some room to ease off." That's calm, not alarming, and it doesn't hand him a worry. Keep it light.

Also, rest that back. Standing for hours is rough on a strain, so sit with your feet up for a bit tonight.
